inputs.text: It's clear that right-wing forces in Cyprus are doubling down on their attack against basic accountability, pushing to strip away judicial oversight in surveillance laws and hand security forces unchecked power. Lawyers sounded the alarm on Monday, and now Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides is stepping up after that closed House session to fight the amended bill. This thing is heading for a vote in the plenum on Thursday, and stopping it is urgent. These kinds of erosions always land hardest on marginalized communities, workers, and progressive voices who already bear the weight of historical and structural oppression. Far from making anyone safer, this move risks weaponizing surveillance to lock in inequality and crush dissent from people facing systemic barriers every day.
